questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the double-entry principle?

options.text: Every transaction affects only one account.
Every transaction affects at least two accounts.
Every transaction is recorded only as a credit.
Every transaction is recorded only as a debit.

questions.explanation: The double-entry principle states that every transaction affects at least two accounts, ensuring the accounting equation remains balanced.

distractorRationale.a: This ignores the requirement for both a debit and a credit entry.
distractorRationale.c: Transactions require both a debit and a credit, not just a credit.
distractorRationale.d: Transactions require both a debit and a credit, not just a debit.

questions.stem: If Chidi pays ₦10,000 in cash for office rent, how should this be recorded?

options.text: Debit Rent Expense ₦10,000; Credit Accounts Payable ₦10,000

questions.explanation: When paying rent, the Rent Expense account is debited because it receives value, and the Cash account is credited because it gives value.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the debit and credit entries.
distractorRationale.c: Accounts Payable is not involved in this cash transaction.
distractorRationale.d: Accounts Payable is not involved in this cash transaction.

questions.stem: What happens to the trial balance when all transactions are correctly recorded using the double-entry system?

options.text: The trial balance will not balance.
The trial balance will have more debits than credits.
The trial balance will have more credits than debits.

questions.explanation: When all transactions are correctly recorded, the total debits will equal the total credits, resulting in a balanced trial balance.

distractorRationale.a: Correct recording ensures the trial balance is balanced.
distractorRationale.b: Debits and credits should be equal, not one more than the other.
distractorRationale.c: Debits and credits should be equal, not one more than the other.

questions.stem: Which account is credited when a business receives cash from a customer for a previous credit sale?
questions.explanation: When cash is received, the Accounts Receivable account is credited because it decreases, reflecting the payment of a previous credit sale.

distractorRationale.a: Cash is debited as it increases with the receipt.
distractorRationale.c: Sales are not affected by the receipt of cash for a previous sale.
distractorRationale.d: Accounts Payable is unrelated to this transaction.

questions.stem: In the double-entry system, every transaction must have at least one debit and one credit entry.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as the double-entry system requires every transaction to be recorded with at least one debit and one credit entry to maintain balance.
